children: By Giancarlo Navach and Giuseppe Fonte
Italy's economy could grow by around 1% this year, above the latest government estimate, Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said on Sunday, as the government is preparing to update its budget plan.
The Italian gross domestic product grew by 0.2% in the second quarter from the previous three ​months, a slightly stronger reading than ‌expected that supports the outlook for this year.

So-called "acquired growth" stood at 0.8% at the end of the April-June period, meaning that even if GDP is flat in each of the remaining two quarters of 2026, full-year growth will be up 0.8% from 2025.
The government estimated growth of 0.6% this year in its multi-year budget framework issued in April.
"If things go as the indicators suggest, we could even get close to 1%," Giorgetti said, addressing the annual TEHA Ambrosetti conference on ⁠the shores of Lake Como.
Italy is due to update its deficit, debt and GDP growth targets later this month.

Giorgetti said he still hoped Eurostat, the EU's statistics office, would revise down last year's deficit-to-GDP ratio to the bloc's 3% ceiling or below from the current 3.1% when it releases updated data on September 22.
Such a revision could pave the way for Italy to exit the European Union's excessive deficit procedure, provided Brussels is convinced the ​improvement in Italy's accounts is persistent.
"I accept the rules. Therefore, if we’re even one thousandth above the limit, we’ll remain in the procedure; if we’re below it, we'll be out of it," Giorgetti said.
He also urged entrepreneurs to raise workers' wages as a way to boost growth.
In recent years Italian wages have risen in nominal terms but less than inflation.
"Business owners need to view wages as one of the primary forms of investment to get the economic cycle back on track," he said.
